newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call rates remain firm despite allocation.
newsitem.headline: German call rates remain firm despite allocation.

text.p: German call rates remained stubbornly high on Wednesday despite a 3.9 billion mark net injection into the banking system at the weekly securities repurchase allocation.
At midday overnight call money traded between 3.15 percent and 3.35 percent, little changed from Tuesday.

Traders said rates were being bid up by expected heavy consumer demand for funds over the Easter holiday and that banks may be forced to increase borrowings at the more expensive 4.50 percent Lombard lending window.
Banks borrowed 2.3 billion marks from the Lombard window on Tuesday.
Traders said call rates could be highly volatile and did not rule out the possibility that overnight money could shoot as high as 4.50 percent.

Credit institutions held 42.9 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Tuesday, up from 40.8 billion marks the day before. The average for the month so far is 40.9 billion marks. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= stood at 3.33500 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.21000 percent on Tuesday. --Frankfurt Newsroom + 49 69 756525
